athlete_inputs.athlete_notes: Vandaag goed ritje met een vriend gereden. Morgen rust en maandag weer werken.

daily_load_assessment: Today's massive load of 182 TSS from a 2.12-hour cycling performance ride, coupled with yesterday's 99 TSS session, represents an extreme back-to-back loading block of 281 TSS. While the subjective feedback notes a 'good ride with a friend,' the physiological cost is exceptionally high relative to your current fitness. Your acute recovery state is severely compromised, with today's fatigue metrics signaling a deep fatigue state. Your subjective desire for recovery tomorrow aligns perfectly with the physiological necessity.
acute_status_assessment_3_weeks: Over the last 21 days, you accumulated 997 TSS over 14.76 hours, with 6 out of 12 sessions classified as high-quality. This has driven your ATL up to 62.98, while your CTL stands at 39.03. This leaves your TSB (Training Stress Balance) at a deep -23.95. This is approaching your absolute limit of -30. Your adaptation rate is under heavy stress; you have successfully stimulated your VO2max and aerobic pathways, but you are now firmly in an overreached state requiring immediate, structured consolidation.
sport_trend_assessment_6_months: The 180-day trend shows a clear transition from sporadic commuting to focused performance efforts. With 26 key cycling sessions in this window, your CTL of 39.03 has been rebuilt quickly. While your FTP (250W, 3.29 W/kg) is solid, your CTL ramp rate has been highly aggressive recently. To safely support cycling torque, running power, and your 5km pace goals, this long-term progression must be stabilized. Your cardiovascular engine is expanding, but your skeletal and muscular structures need a recovery period to absorb this load.
coach_verdict: You executed today's 63.7 km ride at an estimated Intensity Factor (IF) of approximately 0.93. To sustain this level of intensity over more than two hours indicates great mental toughness and a strong anaerobic/VO2max capacity. However, as your coach, I must warn you: back-to-back high-intensity days (yesterday's quality ride + today's demanding group ride) have pushed your fatigue into the red zone. This was a highly productive stimulus, but only if you actually allow your body to supercompensate through strict recovery.

post_workout_recovery.workout_evaluation: You completed 63.7 km in 2.12 hours, averaging ~30 km/h with an exceptionally high load of 182 TSS. This was not a casual cruise; it was a high-tempo, surge-heavy effort that heavily depleted your glycogen stores and taxed your neuromuscular junctions. Compliance with your high-intensity zones was excellent, but the biological debt is high.
post_workout_recovery.hydration_nutrition: Prioritize immediate muscle glycogen restoration and protein synthesis. Consume a recovery shake containing 20g of high-quality whey protein and 60-80g of fast-acting carbohydrates within 30 minutes of finish. Follow up with a whole-food meal featuring complex carbohydrates (sweet potatoes or rice), lean protein (chicken or tofu), and high-sodium electrolytes to replace sweat loss. Drink 1.5 times the fluid weight lost.
post_workout_recovery.stretching_mobility: Focus entirely on the lower chain and thoracic posture to counteract the aggressive cycling position. Perform 3 sets of 45-second holds for: kneeling hip flexor stretch, half-kneeling quad stretch, and pigeon pose for the glutes. Spend 5 minutes on a foam roller releasing the quads, IT bands, and calves to promote venous return.
post_workout_recovery.tomorrow_outlook: Tomorrow is a mandatory, non-negotiable rest day. Your TSB is at -24, meaning your body is in deep repair mode. Expect elevated resting HR and suppressed HRV tomorrow morning. Focus on getting 8.5+ hours of sleep, keeping off your feet, and letting your parasympathetic nervous system take over so you can return to work and training on Monday fully adapted.
